## ⊞  Example Cases

Claim: $n^3 - n$ is divisible by \_\_\_. 

Overview: 

## ⊞  Proof Part 1 (Divisible by \_\_\_): {.smaller}

Consider an arbitrary $n$. Then one of the following must be true

* Case A: $n=3k$

\

* Case B: $n=3k+1$

\

* Case C: $n=3k+2$ 

\

In all 3 cases, $n^3-n$ is divisible by \_\_\_.

## ⊞  Proof Part 2 (Divisible by \_\_\_): {.smaller}

Consider an arbitrary $n$. Then one of the following must be true 

* Case A: $n=2k$

\

* Case B: $n=2k+1$

\

In all 2 cases, $n^3-n$ is divisible by \_\_\_.

Conclusion: 2 and 3 are factors of $n^3-n$ so 6 must be a factor!
